## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 4, entitled *Ukkhittakaosāraṇa* ("Readmitting an ejected nun"), is an ecclesiastical legal text in the Vinaya Piṭaka's analysis of the female monastic disciplinary code [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun who, without authorization from the community, reinstates another nun who has been legitimately suspended or ejected commits an offence entailing initial and subsequent meetings of the Saṅgha (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. The Pali text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. None of the sampled secondary literature passages specifically treat this rule, representing unrelated matches on section symbols [1–22].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral confirm that the rule is shared widely across the Vinaya traditions of different early Buddhist schools [SuttaCentral]. Full parallels survive in the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as the Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha formulations preserved in Chinese (Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Mahāsaṅghika recensions), Tibetan (Mūlasarvāstivāda), and Sanskrit (Lokottaravāda) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus shows 833 matching passages shared across 105 Pali Vinaya texts, with the closest phraseological overlap occurring with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pārājika 7, other *saṅghādisesa* expositions (such as Ss 11, Ss 10, Ss 3, and Ss 13), Khandhaka procedural chapters (Kd 18, Kd 14), and subcommentaries such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007), agreeing with the cross-sectarian transmission of the disciplinary rule [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
